tables.how: The contract numbers and Board file numbers that the case itself prints were read from the case file and looked up: each contract number in the City's Supplier Contracts table, each file number in the Board's legislation records. A further Board file is listed under a contract when its amount before or after equals the contract's agreed amount to the dollar and the two names share a distinctive word, together with the other files of the same agreement. A Board row gives the amount before and after that file, as its title states them; the contract-table row gives the amount agreed today. Three of the Board files are the earlier agreements for the Bayshore Navigation Center, the 260 Golden Gate family shelter and 711 Post Street, which the case sets beside the new agreements.
tables.limits: An increase a department made on its own authority, below the level that needs a vote, leaves no Board file and so no row here: the only trace is the amount before in the next Board file. The contract table keeps today's amount only. A row is a public record of an approval or an amount, not a finding: every increase past $10 million listed here went to the Board, and those acted on were approved. The increases the case describes for Conard House (July 2026), Larkin Street (May 2025 and July 2026) and Urban Alchemy (2024 and 2026) were made without a Board file; they are recited in the Board analyst's reports and the proposed resolutions, and appear here only as the amount before the next Board file.

tables.how: Each agreement of the previous list was set beside every Board file passed before its term began with an amount of $10 million or more. A pair is listed when the file names the same contractor and the two titles share a distinctive word or an abbreviation (for example 'Bayshore', '260', or 'FHSP' for Flexible Housing Subsidy Pool), or when the file names a different contractor and the titles share a street number and one more word. 11 of the 49 new agreements have at least one such earlier file; the case names three of them.
tables.limits: The pairing is by name and title words only and is not confirmed: the City's contract table does not say which agreement a new one replaces, and a provider can run two different programs with similar titles. A new agreement after an old one expires is ordinary; a new agreement begins a new count toward the $10 million level by the Charter's own terms.

sources.t: San Francisco Board of Supervisors: legislation records (Legistar), 2014 to November 2026; each row links to its file

tables.how: Resolutions about a contract, grant or agreement the City pays for, introduced from 1 January to 12 November 2026, whose title gives an amount before of under $10,000,000 and an amount after of $10,000,000 or more: 41 files. The same rule over 2014 to 2026 gives the longer list in the case 'Contracts set just under the $10M Board line, then amended far past it'.
tables.limits: Amounts and names are read by rule from each file's title; the link opens the file itself, which governs. A title shows the latest version of the legislation, and a file that states no earlier amount cannot appear here. Each file is the Board being asked, which is what the Charter requires once an agreement reaches $10 million; several were still pending when the records were retrieved on 13 November 2026.

sources.t: San Francisco Controller: Vendor Payments (Vouchers), fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date (DataSF)

tables.how: Every line of the Controller's payment file, fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2027 to date (to 9 November 2026), added up by payee, department, contract, purchasing rule and year. Two years are shown: the year the voucher was issued, read from its running number (scripts/lib/vouchers.py), and the fiscal year the file lists the line under, which for some lines is later. Kept: the lines that carry the number of a contract the case names or of an agreement in the list of new agreements under the line.
tables.limits: A payment is money paid for work under a contract, not a loss. The payment file starts in July 2018; near the turn of a year the voucher number dates a payment to within a few days.
